name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+15 district with Republican incumbent Jim Baird renominated and seeking re-election
Challenger Drew Cox raised only about $20,000 versus Baird's $358,000 plus over $537,000 in outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic win chance at roughly 4 percent
No public general-election polling; fundamentals point firmly Republican
model.rationale: A fifteen-point Republican district, an incumbent who secured renomination without drama, and a challenger whose campaign has raised roughly a twentieth of Baird's total leave Democrats without a visible path. Prediction markets put the Republican win chance above ninety percent, in line with the district's fundamentals and the lopsided money picture.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal involving Baird, a sudden influx of Democratic outside spending, or unexpected local polling showing a competitive race would move this outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District sits in deeply Republican territory west of Indianapolis, with a partisan lean of roughly fifteen points toward the GOP. Jim Baird, the incumbent congressman, is running for another term after securing renomination, and the district's voters have reliably backed Republicans in House races.

His Democratic opponent, Drew Cox, has run a minimal campaign, reporting about twenty thousand dollars raised and under seven thousand on hand. Baird holds a large financial edge, including more than half a million dollars in outside support, though outside groups have also spent against him. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset, and no public general-election polling is available. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat appears very likely to remain in Republican hands this November.
